## The floor detector and the redo decision {#sec-ch08-redo}

<!-- PROVENANCE
pin: snapy@e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0 (chengcli/snapy)
sources: OUTLINE.md 8.12
status: draft
-->

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
- Detection, not repair: it decides whether the step just taken should be redone.
- A primitive at or below $1.001$ times a floor counts as a hit.
- The marks set by the limiter passes are read alongside it.
- The detector's own restore must not mark a repair, so the marks are reset around it.
:::

Everything else in this chapter keeps the state admissible or records that it could not. This is the
mechanism that decides the step was bad enough to take again, and it is the closest thing snapy has to a
positivity failure path.

### Derivation

The test is a margin above the floor rather than equality with it, at
`hit` ([`meshblock.cpp:1199-1202`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L1199-L1202)): a minimum density at or below $1.001$ times the density floor
counts as a hit, and the same for pressure where there is a pressure row. Testing equality with the
floor would miss a cell that was floored and then nudged by a later operation; the margin catches the
neighbourhood of the floor instead.

The ordering around it carries a subtlety the code calls out at
`reset_limiter_marks` ([`meshblock.cpp:1259-1261`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L1259-L1261)): the detector restores primitives in order to look at them, and
that restore itself runs a conversion which can trip the limiter and set a mark. The marks are therefore
reset so that the detector's own work is not mistaken for a repair of the step being judged.

### Numerical method

The detector is `hydro_u` ([`meshblock.cpp:1190-1204`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L1190-L1204)). The marks are read through
`limiter_hits` ([`meshblock.cpp:1211-1218`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L1211-L1218)), which returns the pair set by the limiter passes of
@sec-ch08-eoslimiter, and the implicit clamp of @sec-ch08-vic is read through its own accessor at
`vic_dry_clamp_hit` ([`meshblock.cpp:1206-1208`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L1206-L1208)). The redo decision combines them at
[`meshblock.cpp:1276-1281`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L1276-L1281), where the floor test is run first and the marks are read
afterwards, in that order, for the reason above.

### Tests

No test in the repository isolates the detector. It is written here from reading.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- A redo repeats the step; it does not make the step succeed. A column that floors at every step size
  will keep flooring, and the redo budget of the time-integration chapter is what ends the loop.
:::

1. **The margin is a constant.** The factor $1.001$ is not derived and not configurable. A cell
   legitimately sitting a tenth of a per cent above the floor is read as a hit.
2. **Detection is per block.** One floored cell marks the whole block for a redo, and nothing records
   which cell it was.
